title: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (2007), Beginners' Guide to Financial Statement
use: Dated investor-education orientation to balance sheets, income statements, cash-flow statements, equity changes and explanatory notes. Harbor's recognition conventions and numerical cases are original and separately stipulated.
verification: Actual official HTML body inspected, principal statements and their connections, balance-sheet equation, period-versus-date distinction and notes discussion. Page reports February 2007 publication/update. Used as elementary orientation, not a current accounting standard. The chapter does not adopt the guide's informal liquidation shorthand as an equality between recorded equity and realizable sale proceeds, or describe all expenses as contemporaneous cash payments.

title: IFRS Foundation, IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows — public standard overview
use: Operating/investing/financing categories, direct and indirect operating methods, cash perimeter, separate noncash investing/financing disclosure and acknowledgement of IFRS 18-related amendments.
verification: Actual accessible official overview body inspected under About, including activity/method descriptions, noncash exclusions and cash reconciliation; standards-history paragraph records April 2024 IFRS 18 amendments. Full IAS 7 publication route required subscription access; no full normative-text inspection is claimed and no access-control workaround was used. The chapter's interest/dividend and profit-start conventions are maintained case assumptions, not a universal statement of current IFRS requirements.

title: Paul Munter, SEC Chief Accountant (4 December 2023), The Statement of Cash Flows: Improving the Quality of Cash Flow Information Provided to Investors
use: Importance of cash-flow classification, noncash transaction disclosure and controls beyond reconciling total cash; motivates original wrong-classification and balanced-wrong-recognition counterexamples.
verification: Actual official staff-statement body inspected, introductory classification discussion, noncash disclosure and controls sections, direct-method discussion and footnote 1. The footnote identifies this as staff views without Commission rule status or new legal force. The chapter retains that qualification; it does not claim to have independently inspected all cited ASC provisions or reproduce the statement's restatement-frequency statistics.

title: IFRS Foundation (April 2024), New IFRS Accounting Standard will aid investor analysis of companies' financial performance
use: Exact IFRS 18 effective-date distinction: annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with earlier application permitted; explains why a 2025 teaching case cannot silently stand in for every later framework/version.
verification: Actual official issuance announcement body inspected, including effective-date and early-application paragraph. The claim concerns the standard's stated date, not adoption by every jurisdiction or any specific company's reporting elections. No current company adoption data are supplied or inferred.

title: IFRS Foundation (April 2024), IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements — Effects Analysis, page 27
use: Explains IFRS 18-related IAS 7 changes to the indirect method's starting subtotal and interest/dividend cash-flow classification, and why income-statement categories must not automatically determine cash-flow categories.
verification: Actual official 64-page PDF extracted body inspected at printed page 27 (physical page 26), Improving comparability of cash flow information and accompanying category discussion/table. Public effects analysis is explanatory material, not the full normative standard. The chapter states the existence and nature of amendments without claiming a comprehensive treatment of entity-specific investing/financing main-business exceptions.
